requirement: Implement SafeBatchExecutor with execute_batch partitioning successes and failures, using return_exceptions=True or fail-fast sibling cancellation with first-exception semantics.
skeleton: Asyncio batch task runner partitioning successes, failures, and handling sibling task cancellation.
caption: A pure-asyncio batch executor with no third-party imports. BatchExecutionResult is a dataclass with a successes list, a failures list typed as BaseException, and a cancelled_count integer, each list built by default_factory. SafeBatchExecutor.execute_batch takes a list of zero-argument coroutine factories and a cancel_siblings_on_error flag defaulting to False, and returns an empty result for an empty list. In the default mode it awaits asyncio.gather over every factory's coroutine with return_exceptions=True, so a raising task does not abort the gather, then walks the raw results in order: an asyncio.CancelledError instance increments cancelled_count, any other BaseException instance is appended to failures, and everything else is appended to successes. In fail-fast mode it wraps each coroutine in asyncio.create_task, awaits asyncio.wait with return_when set to FIRST_EXCEPTION, and inspects the done set: when some finished task holds an exception and others are still pending, every pending task is cancelled and then gathered with return_exceptions=True so the cancellations settle; when nothing failed, the pending set is awaited to completion instead. The tasks are then classified in submission order by task.cancelled(), task.exception(), and task.result() into the same three buckets. A ValueError or RuntimeError raised by one task therefore lands in failures as an exception object, never in successes, a sibling cancelled after the first failure is counted rather than filed as a failure, and a long-running sibling in fail-fast mode is actually stopped rather than left running in the background.

plan.intent: Execute a batch of coroutines and classify every outcome
constraints: The default mode gathers with exceptions returned so one failure never aborts the batch
Failures are kept as exception objects and never counted as successes
Fail-fast mode cancels still-pending siblings after the first exception and waits for them to settle
Cancelled tasks are counted separately from failures
An empty batch returns an empty result

rationale.teaches: Batch execution with gather: return_exceptions=True to partition results, exceptions routed to failures, cancellations counted separately, and pending siblings cancelled in fail-fast mode.
rationale.why: gather's two modes look alike until one task raises. Whether siblings keep running, whether the exception is lost, and whether it is misfiled are only visible with a deliberately failing task.

ops.docstring: Run a batch of coroutines and sort every outcome into successes and failures.

ops.source: type TaskFactory = Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]]

candidates.why_wrong: return_exceptions=False makes the first exception propagate out of gather, so no partition is ever produced.
Exceptions are appended to successes, so a batch with failures reports every task as succeeded.
Exceptions are silently dropped, so failures is always empty and the caller never learns a task failed.
Cancelled tasks are appended to failures instead of counted, so cancelled_count stays 0 and failures over-reports.
Pending siblings are not cancelled after the first failure, so fail-fast mode leaves tasks running in the background.
